doc.title: Josiah Gluck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 13, 2022

title: Early fascination with technology and radio; live mishaps
summary: He loved music and gadgets from age five, discovered in college radio that they could combine, and notes live failures are handled by rolling with them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So music and technology go hand-in-hand in your work. And I’m curious, when you were young which of those things seemed to attract you.

You know I would have to say it was both things. I’ve always loved music and from the time I was I don’t know five years old or so TVs, record players, movie projectors, all that sort of stuff just fascinated me and I always wanted to know how does this work, how does that happen, how do you deal with sirens going by? You know. I’ve just always loved that. And somehow this revealed itself to me I guess in college that you could combine these things. I mean I played around with tape recorders and trying to record stuff in high school but it was really working at a radio station in college that I got to do a lot of hands-on work with technology.
And I’m going to assume dealing with dead air and things that go awry in a live situation?

They can happen. Yes. I’m actually kind of surprised that they don’t happen more often because there’s so much at stake. We’ve had our share of mishaps whether or not it’s during a sketch or something with music. That’s also why we have dress rehearsals, to see where there could be a possible problem. But there have been failures on-air and you just roll with them. You just have to deal with it.
